name: Stefan Brandt
why: A physicist’s cotton jersey — Peruvian Pima spun and finished to his own recipe, cut into tees, jersey shirts and polos that hold their shape after the machine.
origin: Stefan Brandt, Germany — a physicist who left science to make jersey to his own tolerances, supplying the cloth to other houses as well as cutting his own.
opview: Positions itself as luxury defined by material and fit rather than logo.

onething.n: A collared shirt cut from his fine Pima jersey — hand-set collar and placket, washable at 40°. Read on Breuninger; no US store.

notes.reach: Two US stockists on the register — Richards, Greenwich and Maxwell & Co., Falmouth — no US store, no US e-commerce. Seated 26 Sep 2026 on Sebastian’s sighting.
notes.tech: Names its own jersey (Urpima cotton, a Prefit finishing process) and supplies it to other houses; ownership is the house’s. Scored provisionally at 3 pending the tech re-score.
notes.fuss: Read on Breuninger (EUR) 26 Sep 2026; the house has no US store. Jeans and shoes: does not make. Dress pants: sweat trousers only, not read. Machine-washable at 40° and dryer-safe is the house’s own claim.

doors.basis: positive zero, 26 Sep 2026: no US own store

cities: Greenwich & Falmouth · two specialists, no US store
